title: Helicity-Defined Persistent Analog Memory
question: Can optical helicity program durable analog states that remain electrically distinguishable in an addressed array?
teaser: Optical helicity programs persistent conductance states that remain electrically readable in a device array.
mechanism: Chirality-matched circularly polarized light conditions persistent conductance updates in layered chiral perovskite synapses.
approach: Measure state separability and retention, then evaluate a PCB-integrated 7 × 7 device array with ADC/FPGA readout.
evidence: State-resolved retention and read-noise analysis; array conductance maps and mixed-signal vector–matrix multiplication.
achievement: 72 statistically distinguishable states through 10⁶ s · 7 × 7 array · PCB-integrated readout.
myContribution: Co-first author; the publisher credits conceptualization, methodology, investigation, data curation, and original-draft writing.
outcome: Helicity-conditioned states remained circuit-readable through PCB-based array addressing and digitization.
